text:
mike: Heads-up: after rolling AWQ37 on mistral-14b-prod we saw 2x p99 on long-seq < 2k tokens during KV warmup. Repro steps + perf trace below, looks like kernel choice is flipping mid-request and killing microbatching.
ana: Can you paste the trace? is this only AWQ or also GPTQ builds?
mike: only AWQ37 so far. Trace snippet: ```
[pid:1234] seq=1536 init-kv-hit=0 choose-kernel=awq_int8_opt -> fallback=fp8_vecloop at token 7 -> batch-flush
[batcher] soft-limit=32 current=28 flush_reason=slew
``` 
perf-bot: Profiling summary (quick): AWQ int8 kernel has 18% faster per-token in steady-state but 60-120ms extra tail when kernel fallback happens. KV cache miss penalty amplified for long rotary windows. Full flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/trace/2559876543
shivani: Accuracy-wise we measured +0.6 BLEU drop on our calibration set (conversational prompts) with the default AWQ params. Calib prompts where distribution has long context + many repeated tokens amplify per-head quantization noise.
taylor: Hypothesis: RoPE scale matrix mismatch across head dims causing some heads to underflow when quantized -> kernel detects instability and falls back. Also batching flush logic is too eager when a kernel switch happens.
ana: Can you try forcing the AWQ kernel affinity to remain for the whole request (no mid-request kernel arbitration) and see? we can add a runtime flag like `runtime.force_kernel_stickiness=true`.
mike: I ran `./tools/perf_run --model mistral-14b-awq --seq 2048 --batcher soft=32 --force-stick` and saw p99 back to normal but 7% aggregate latency increase (due to AWQ pathological frames). Command pasted:
```
./tools/perf_run \
  --model mistral-14b-awq \
  --quant awq37 \
  --seq-len 2048 \
  --concurrency 4 \
  --batcher-soft 32 \
  --force-kernel-stickiness
```
perf-bot: Quick metric snapshot after `force-stick`: p50 +5ms, p99 -40ms, cpu-util +6%, memory unchanged.
shivani: If stickiness helps latency but hurts throughput a bit, we could instead: tune batching heuristic to prefer stable kernel selections for in-flight microbatches. Something like `batcher.prefer_kernel_stable=true` and `batcher.flush_penalty_ms=45`.
taylor: Also let's add a short calibration pass: run 256 calibration prompts with dynamic-range-aware centroids to re-evaluate AWQ scales for rotary-sensitive heads. I can queue that on staging.
ana: We should also check per-head magnitude distributions. If some heads are near zero mean after RoPE rescale, AWQ may collapse them. Can we dump head stats from the loader? simple script:
```
python -c "from loader import Model; m=Model('mistral-14b'); print(m.head_stats())"
```
mike: I dumped them. Most heads look ok but heads 9, 22 show std dev ~0.02 vs others ~0.12. Attached sample: head9 tail-kv-values clustered -> quant bins hit ceiling.
shivani: Proposed plan: (1) run head-level calibration for AWQ on the 256 prompts (2) add kernel stickiness opt behind feature flag (3) soften batcher flush threshold and add penalty for kernel switches (4) validate with perf harness and accuracy eval.
taylor: I'll implement the batcher change: heuristics: when a candidate kernel change is detected, hold microbatch for up to N ms (default 50) if that avoids flushing and retains at least 80% latency SLO. Pseudocode:
```
if kernel_change_detected:
  if holding_time < batcher.switch_hold_ms:
    wait_for_more_requests()
  else:
    flush()
```
mike: One more: could FP8 fallback be made less aggressive? maybe only fallback if >3 consecutive unstable tokens rather than single token flip.
ana: Good call. Add `kernel.fallback_threshold=3` behind flag.
perf-bot: I've scheduled a rolling canary with flags: `force-stick=false`, `batcher.switch_hold_ms=50`, `kernel.fallback_threshold=3`, AWQ head-calib=on. Canary starts in 5m.
mike: Thanks. Will monitor traces; if p99 doesn't regress we'll promote. If latency improves but accuracy drops >1.5% we'll rollback.
shivani: I'll run the calibration eval and post numbers in #eng-ml once done.
taylor: Will open PR for the batcher change and feature flags. small note: add metrics `kernel_switches_per_minute` & `batch_flush_reasons` so we can alert on regressions.
mike: Awesome. If anyone spots a model where RoPE scale differs from our baseline mapping (mistral vs mixtral head-depth), call it out here.
ana: noted. :eyes:
